clue.text: That non-binary person's put on lingerie items — they're striped

indicators.note: one piece is placed on the other, so the pronoun comes before the underwear

parts.note: ze is a gender-neutral pronoun some non-binary people use; the 's is read as 'is'
bras are items of women's underwear

explanation.surface: Someone is getting dressed in a set of underwear, which turns out to have stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little phrase rather than a noun, but 'they're striped' fairly describes the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Zebras are African wild horses famous for their black-and-white stripes.

clue.text: A hundred bundles of paper bags

parts.note: taken as written
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A stationery order: a hundred packs of paper sacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a plural noun, but it is a verb, as in bagging a seat; C is the Roman numeral for a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is informally to get hold of it or claim it, which is to obtain it.

clue.text: Land in the main depressed after sensational story

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun; the main is the open sea

indicators.note: the word for 'depressed' is placed after the sensational story

parts.note: a splash is a big front-page newspaper story
feeling down means feeling low

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy after reading a lurid tabloid story about something landing in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, so this is the landing of a spacecraft in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a spacecraft's landing in the sea at the end of a mission.

clue.text: Politician holding male member

indicators.note: the politician's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician in custody of a man who belongs to some body.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb, such as an arm or leg, is one of the body's members.

clue.text: Liven up, mad about northern Spanish city

indicators.note: the word for 'mad' goes around the other letters

parts.note: mad in the sense of angry
Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain

explanation.surface: An angry tourist wants to brighten up a city in northern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to give energy or vitality to, to enliven.

clue.text: Ignoring United, a Chelsea player with talent

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for United is ignored, so it is dropped

parts.note: Chelsea FC play in blue and are nicknamed the Blues

explanation.surface: A football pundit praises a skilful Chelsea footballer while setting Manchester United aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea are a London football club; their players are called Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able is capable and skilled, possessing talent.

clue.text: Live wire in party drinking a great deal, tipping over

indicators.note: the party takes in the other letters as if swallowing them

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the word is tipped over, so read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: many means a great deal of

explanation.surface: An energetic guest at a party is drinking a lot and knocking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: A live wire, with its electrical surface, points to the generator; here it means an energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an energetic, forceful person, just as a live wire is someone full of energy.

clue.text: Using computers in nuanced piece of translation

indicators.note: the computers piece goes in the word for nuanced

parts.note: something subtle is finely nuanced
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Using machine translation on a subtle passage of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtitle is a caption translating a film's dialogue for viewers in another language.

clue.text: Republican expelled from party admitting vote anomaly

indicators.note: the shortened party lets the vote in
Republican's letter is thrown out of the party

parts.note: a reception is a formal party
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A Republican is thrown out of the party while an odd vote is let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics alongside Republican, but here it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An exception is a case that does not follow the rule, an irregularity.

clue.text: Horse outside of Ouagadougou in marshy area

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

indicators.note: only the outside letters, first and last, of the city's name are used

parts.note: the capital of Burkina Faso, used only for its outer letters

explanation.surface: A horse is wading through a swamp outside the capital of Burkina Faso.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayou is a slow, marshy stretch of water in the southern United States, especially Louisiana.

clue.text: What may make a fool vocally regret harsh remark

definitions.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream dessert

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for regret gives the sound of the first syllable

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a cutting comment that made somebody look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream; this plant is a classic choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb stalks are stewed and folded into cream to make the pudding called rhubarb fool.

clue.text: I demand to follow initiator of nouvelle vague

indicators.note: the demand word follows the earlier letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the French word supplies just its opening letter
to exact is to demand

explanation.surface: A film director insists on following the pioneer of the French New Wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nouvelle vague' is French cinema's New Wave, but 'vague' here is the English word and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise or not definite, like a vague answer.

clue.text: What to call a baronet right behind one's back

indicators.note: the right letter comes behind the reversed piece
the letters for one's are read back to front

parts.note: one's is short for 'one is', I IS

explanation.surface: Gossip about how one addresses a baronet behind his back.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet is addressed by the title Sir before his first name, like a knight.

clue.text: Endlessly discuss Marx and forbid doing a U-turn on strike

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team

indicators.note: the word for forbid turns round and runs backwards

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: Talk about Karl Marx, banning things and strikes goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl, but it is Harpo, the silent Marx Brother.
explanation.definitionFit: To harp on about something is to keep talking about it tediously, without letting up.

clue.text: Dogs from Liverpool entertaining me

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds
the compiler of the crossword is its setter, speaking of himself as 'me'

explanation.surface: Some dogs from Liverpool are amusing the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' reads as amusing, but it means holding inside; crossword setters often call themselves 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red setters, also called Irish setters, are a breed of gundog with glossy chestnut coats.

clue.text: Coming before e.g. worker seeking love online?

parts.note: a worker ant is one example of a worker
e-dating is finding romance through the internet; the question mark flags the coinage

explanation.surface: An example of a working person looking for romance on a dating site.
explanation.definitionFit: Antedating something means preceding it in time, occurring earlier than it.

clue.text: Financial associates concealing way to seize stock

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer across their join

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of financial and the start of associates

explanation.surface: Business partners are hiding a method for taking over company shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' and 'Financial' point to shares, but this stock is livestock on a ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used by cowboys for catching cattle and horses.

clue.text: Old French bread Parisian agreed to feed to dissolute lords

indicators.note: the word for yes is fed into the rearranged letters
dissolute means loose-living, so the letters are loosened and reordered

parts.note: the letters of lords are the fodder, used as written
oui is French for yes

explanation.surface: A Parisian kindly agrees to give a loaf to some debauched aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so the definition is an old French coin, not a baguette.
explanation.definitionFit: The louis d'or was a gold coin of France from Louis XIII until the Revolution; bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Make-up from the east in handbag

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left
the letters sit inside the word handbag

parts.note: the three letters sit in the middle of the word handbag

explanation.surface: Cosmetics from the Orient are kept in a lady's handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics in a handbag; it is genetic make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA carries the genetic code that determines an organism's inherited constitution.

clue.text: Prime heroin loaded aboard plane?

indicators.note: the drug is loaded inside the plane's letters

parts.note: a plane is a tree; the question mark flags the deception
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: First-rate heroin is smuggled onto an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft, but it is the plane tree; 'Prime' means a prime number.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a prime number, divisible only by itself and one.

clue.text: Nastier manoeuvres keeping king in check

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the king inside them
the word's letters are manoeuvred into a new order

parts.note: the word nastier is the fodder, used as written
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A chess game where nasty moves keep the opponent's king in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'check' look like a chess term; it is a verb meaning hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep under control, which is to check.

clue.text: Fanciful story Pope, say, penned in advance

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes

indicators.note: the abbreviation is penned in, enclosed within the other word

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A tall tale about the Pope writing something ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope, say' looks like an example indicator for the Pope, but 'say' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban legend is a widely circulated but untrue story presented as fact.

clue.text: Inspirational figure to join the Tories

parts.note: to join a group is to be a member of it
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A charismatic leader signs up with the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'be a Con': joining the Tories makes you a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a guiding light, figuratively a person who inspires or guides others.

clue.text: Show unhappiness with scoundrel from America

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., the American initials for 'son of a bitch'

explanation.walkthrough: The American sense is an abbreviation for a coarse insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to weep convulsively, and in US slang an SOB is a contemptible person.

clue.text: Most contemptible guitar player in recital

indicators.note: in recital means spoken aloud, so the sound gives the answer

parts.note: a bassist plays the bass guitar

explanation.surface: A critic damns the worst bass guitarist performing at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recital' suggests a concert, but it signals the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Basest is the superlative of base, meaning morally low or despicable.

clue.text: Red Sierra — diminutive vehicle?

explanation.surface: A red Ford Sierra, which is perhaps a rather small car.

explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright, vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Pool ball under cover

clue.text: Trainees put in the ground shell of nuts

clue.text: British capital raised, taking lead from Michael Foot

indicators.note: the raised letters take in the Michael letter

parts.note: the name supplies only its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the Labour Party; here 'Foot' is the metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of an unstressed then a stressed syllable.

clue.text: Latin writer penning nothing elliptical

indicators.note: the writer pens, enclosing, the zero

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elliptical' suggests terse writing, but it means egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, an oval form like an ellipse.

clue.text: People like Byron love getting stuck into jollies and capers
